scope.question: which reproducible keys identify this build, and which of them are unavailable
scope.authenticator_skipped_reason: chain validation can trigger revocation traffic; the run stays offline, so only bytes the signature already contains are compared

pdb_availability.symbol_resolution_reason: no PDB matching the embedded GUID and age exists in the workspace, so no function, type or source line name can be attached to any address in this evidence set

linker.linker_version_semantics: the PE field is an MSVC compatible value that lld-link has written for years; it is not a release number and it is overridable at link time

pe_timestamp.reproducible_build_note: the COFF timestamp is writable by the linker, so it is a comparison value, not a provenance proof

build_id.lld_build_id_reason: PE/COFF has no standard build id field and lld-link emits none for PE targets, so no linker identity record survives here; the only uppercase `LLD ` byte occurrence sits inside the CodeView GUID field, which is a GUID byte coincidence, not a marker

rich_header.consequence: no Rich build id, no compiler or product tuple and no Visual Studio toolchain version is recoverable from this specimen

retpolne.interpretation: LLD COFF retpoline metadata marker. Only the byte positions and words are reported here; the record layout is not decoded, so the tag count is a raw fact and not a record count.

linker.lld_release_reason: no linker identity record survives in the image; see build_id.lld_build_id_reason and rich_header.consequence

identity_resources.version_layers_note: the PE version and the FXCOMPONENT version are separate resource types and are not cross-linked in the specimen

embedded_build_paths.extraction_rule: NUL terminated printable ASCII runs of 8..300 bytes that start with `C:\gl\` or `..\`

image_digest.section_region: full SizeOfRawData per section, section table order
image_digest.cryptographic_operation: none; this is a byte recomputation, not a signature verification and not a statement about chain validity

certificate_table.verification_note: no chain validation and no revocation lookup is performed here, so nothing is asserted about signer identity, chain validity or revocation status; only bytes the signature already contains are compared

excluded_from_provenance_scan.Bin/** (non-config): opaque vendor binaries; covered by module name resolution only, their own identity is out of scope here
excluded_from_provenance_scan.build/: generated CMake output, reproducible from the sources above
excluded_from_provenance_scan.reverse/*.md: sibling analysis reports; they are the output of this evidence set, not a build-provenance source

workspace.ambient_naming_note: fivem and citizenfx hits come from the C++ `namespace fivem`, the project name and product prose; they are not build-provenance references to the specimen

pdb_inventory.symbol_resolution_reason: no PDB matching the embedded GUID and age exists in the workspace, so no function, type or source line name can be attached to any address in this evidence set

import_module_resolution.note: the workspace Bin/ tree is the FXServer payload set while the specimen is a client component, so a partial overlap is expected and does not establish a shared build

recompute_recipe.pdb_debug_id: uppercase RSDS GUID without dashes, then the age as uppercase hex
recompute_recipe.pdb_match_key: sha256 of b'\x00'.join([lowercased pdb path with '/' replaced by '\\', guid_bytes_le, little-endian age])
recompute_recipe.authenticode_image_sha256: sha256 over bytes [0, SizeOfHeaders) minus the 4 byte CheckSum field and the 8 byte Security directory entry, then each section's full SizeOfRawData in section table order
recompute_recipe.section_table_key: sha256 of sorted 'name|rva|vsize|rawptr|rawsize|characteristics|raw_sha256' lines, LF terminated
recompute_recipe.section_content_key: sha256 of sorted 'name#content_sha256' lines over the first min(SizeOfRawData, VirtualSize) bytes of each section
recompute_recipe.import_symbols_key: sha256 of sorted 'dll!symbol' lines, ordinal imports written as 'dll!#ordinal'
recompute_recipe.build_path_corpus_key: sha256 of sorted 'abs:<path>' and 'rel:<path>' lines for every extracted build path
recompute_recipe.correlation_vector_sha256: sha256 of the compact sorted-key JSON of all other keys except whole_file_size and pdb_path

authenticity.component_identification_basis: CreateComponent export, FXCOMPONENT resource, CitizenFX version resource and the FiveM client import set
authenticity.statement: This artifact set does not assert that the specimen is an authentic vendor build. Component identity is established from the bytes; build provenance is not. The embedded Authenticode digest equals the recomputed PE image hash, which shows only that the signed bytes are the present bytes. No signature chain was validated, no PDB was located, and no second artifact of the same build exists in this workspace, so there is nothing to compare the debug ID or the section keys against.
requirements_to_lift: locate adhesive.pdb with debug id CB927E363F3D8D774C4C44205044422E1 and age 1, verify its own stream identity, and resolve symbols through it
obtain a second artifact of the same 1.0.0.36109 build and compare correlation_vector_sha256
verify the Authenticode chain in a separate network-permitted step and record the verification result together with its timestamp
obtain the official build manifest that maps build number 36109 to a published artifact

open_questions.question: Where is adhesive.pdb with debug id CB927E363F3D8D774C4C44205044422E1 and age 1, and can symbols be resolved through it?
open_questions.why_it_matters: without the PDB no function, type or source line name can be attached to any address in this evidence set
open_questions.closes_when: the matching PDB is located and its stream identity is verified, or a symbol server entry is confirmed absent

open_questions.question: Which official artifact corresponds to build 36109 of the CitizenFX 1.0.0.36109 client?
open_questions.why_it_matters: the embedded PDB path names a build cache root, not a release; the PE version, the FXCOMPONENT version and the build number live in three different layers and are not cross-linked anywhere
open_questions.closes_when: an official build manifest or a second signed artifact of the same build number is available for comparison

open_questions.question: Which exact LLVM LLD release performed the final link?
open_questions.why_it_matters: the 14.0 linker field is an MSVC 2015 compatibility value, the Rich header is absent, and no build id survives, so the retpoline metadata is a behavioural fingerprint only
open_questions.closes_when: a build log, a reproducible rebuild with a pinned linker, or a toolchain marker from a same-family artifact becomes available

open_questions.question: Was the MSVC or the clang-cl frontend used, and which runtime build?
open_questions.why_it_matters: both frontends produce the observed MSVC compatible ABI, dynamic MSVC/UCRT imports and load config layout, so the specimen cannot distinguish them
open_questions.closes_when: a toolchain fingerprint from a same-family artifact or a build log identifies frontend and CRT version

open_questions.question: Does the retpolne tag count of 4 (section offsets 0x0, 0x10, 0x2C, 0x40) contradict the peer report value of 3, or does that report count record pairs instead of tags?
open_questions.why_it_matters: a tag count disagreement is a raw byte level conflict and must be settled before the section is used as a differential key between builds
open_questions.closes_when: the retpolne record layout is decoded and the peer report is corrected or confirmed

open_questions.question: Why do 276 of the 278 embedded absolute build paths sit under vendor/, and only one under code/client/?
open_questions.why_it_matters: retention of __FILE__ strings is a compiler and optimisation level property, and the ratio constrains which claims about first-party source layout are supportable
open_questions.closes_when: the set of translation units that emit __FILE__ under this toolchain is characterised, or a same-family build is compared

open_questions.question: Is the specimen from the same build campaign as the FXServer payload in Bin/, given that Bin/components.json lists server components and does not list adhesive, and several declared client modules are absent from Bin/?
open_questions.why_it_matters: the workspace and the specimen are different product surfaces; correlating their build numbers without evidence would be a provenance error
open_questions.closes_when: the build numbers of the Bin/ payload artifacts are extracted and compared against 36109

open_questions.question: What is the version relationship between the PE version 1.0.0.36109 and the FXCOMPONENT version 0.1.0?
open_questions.why_it_matters: both are component scoped yet stored in different resource types, and a correlation key that mixes them would be unstable across builds
open_questions.closes_when: two or more builds show whether the FXCOMPONENT version is bumped independently of the PE version

open_questions.question: Is the embedded build path root C:\gl\builds\cfx-fivem-0 a stable CI worker path or a per-agent path?
open_questions.why_it_matters: a stable root makes the PDB path usable as a build key; a per-agent path makes it noise that must stay out of correlation vectors
open_questions.closes_when: two builds of the same component are compared and the path roots are shown to be identical or divergent

open_questions.question: Do the section content hashes stay stable across rebuilds of the same build number, or does build-local absolute path material from .build-cache leak into .rdata and break the key?
open_questions.why_it_matters: the section keys only serve build-to-build correlation if they are insensitive to the build directory layout
open_questions.closes_when: two artifacts of the same build number are compared at section level and the keys are either equal or the difference is explained

open_questions.question: Is the two digit year signingTime encoding inside the timestamp token byte-identical to the four digit year representation found in the same certificate table?
open_questions.why_it_matters: two representations of the same instant in one blob affects which one a downstream tool treats as authoritative
open_questions.closes_when: both encodings are decoded and compared, and the timestamp token structure is documented

reproduce.external_inputs: none; the script reads the specimen, common.py and the workspace tree only

cross_check.note: independent parse of the same bytes, compared against the stored baseline; a mismatch means the specimen or the parser changed
